- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% if recent price is falling.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day mean, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is weak or mixed, model often misses downward trend; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias if sentiment <0.4 for 3+ days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend if sentiment shifts sharply.
